title: The Best Sum With a Length Between L and R

concept.title: A sliding window minimum over the prefix sums
body: Find the largest sum of a subarray whose length is **at least `lo` and at most `hi`**. With prefix sums `P`, a subarray that ends at `j` (it covers `a[x..j-1]`) has the sum `P[j] - P[x]` and the length `j - x`. For a fixed end `j`, the allowed starts are `x` from `j - hi` to `j - lo`. The best subarray for this end uses the **smallest `P[x]`** in that range of starts. As `j` grows by one, the range of starts moves by one: a **sliding window** minimum over `P`.

The sliding window minimum is the classic job of a **monotonic deque**: keep the indexes with increasing `P` values. When `j` increases, add the new start `j - lo` (remove from the back all with `P` not smaller than the new one), and remove from the front the starts that are older than `j - hi`. The front is the minimum.

body.code:
best = -inf; dq = deque()
for j in range(lo, n + 1):
    s = j - lo                                   # the newest allowed start
    while dq and P[dq[-1]] >= P[s]: dq.pop()
    dq.append(s)
    while dq[0] < j - hi: dq.popleft()           # too far: the subarray would be too long
    best = max(best, P[j] - P[dq[0]])

body: The deque is never empty after the push, because the newest start `j - lo` is always allowed (`lo <= hi`). The sums are large (`20000 * 10^9`), so use 64-bit integers.

statement: Given `n` integers (they may be negative) and two numbers `lo` and `hi`, find the largest sum of a contiguous subarray whose length is at least `lo` and at most `hi`. Print this sum.

examples.note: The subarray 3 4 has length 2 and the sum 7. A subarray of length 3 reaches at most 6.

hints: Use prefix sums: for an end j the sum is P[j] - P[x] with x between j - hi and j - lo.
You need the smallest P[x] in a window that moves to the right.
A monotonic deque of indexes gives the minimum of a sliding window in O(1) per step.

explanation: With prefix sums, the best subarray ending at j starts at the minimum prefix sum among the allowed starts. A monotonic deque maintains this minimum while the window of starts slides to the right.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, lo, hi = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

from collections import deque

prefix = [0] * (n + 1)
for i in range(n):
    prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + a[i]
dq = deque()
best = None
for j in range(lo, n + 1):
    s = j - lo
    while dq and prefix[dq[-1]] >= prefix[s]:
        dq.pop()
    dq.append(s)
    while dq[0] < j - hi:
        dq.popleft()
    value = prefix[j] - prefix[dq[0]]
    if best is None or value > best:
        best = value
print(best)
